historical_record.description: The Board of Permit Appeals upheld the Department of Public Works' denial of a permit to erect a structure at 2925 California Street, the appeal being denied for lack of the required four overrule votes, with a rehearing automatically granted for November 30, 1977 because the vote of the absent commissioner might have changed the result.

The Board of Permit Appeals overruled the Department of Public Works' denial of a permit to erect a structure at 2925 California Street on rehearing, with the intent that the appellant be granted a permit to build six dwelling units, and with stipulations that the appellant comply with all City code requirements and procedures necessary to perfect the permit, including the filing of an environmental evaluation report, and conform as closely as possible to the principles outlined in the study "Change Without Loss: Residential Development and Preservation for San Francisco Neighborhoods".
